units.text: INT. CURLING RINK - PRE-DAWN
A tin-roofed rink in a Manitoba grain town, the ice a long pale sheet scored by a thousand rocks.
Breath hangs in the cold.
Somewhere a compressor thrums like a heart beneath the floor.
RAINE KOWALCHUK, 40s, the skip, kneels at the hack with her broom across her knees, studying the far house as though it owed her money.
TEODORA BRZEZINSKI, 60s, the coach, leans on the boards in a parka the colour of canned peaches, thermos steaming.

PRIYA NAIR, 20s, the lead, sweeps a pebble from the lane with great ceremony, while WALT DUNPHY, 70, the second, lowers himself onto a bench with a groan like a gate, and SUNDAY ADEYEMI, 30s, the third, rests her chin on her broom handle and watches the three of them as if counting something.
Everything is calm.
Even the compressor seems to hush.
Draw weight's fine. Ice is keen. You'll hit the button on the last end like you've done ten thousand times.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: We're not at the last end.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: We will be.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: Eleven-nine, they said. Eleven-nine and we're the underdogs. Never been an underdog. I was always the old dog.
units.name: WALT

units.text: You're still the old dog, Walt.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Language.
units.name: WALT

units.text: Raine. You haven't said a word about the match.
units.name: SUNDAY

units.text: Didn't think I needed to.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: You always have a word about the match.
units.name: SUNDAY

units.text: Fine. I have a word. After today I'm not skipping.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: You're saying you want to throw last stones. I can arrange that.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: I'm saying I'm done, Teo. Not skipping. Not anything. After today I'm gone. Winnipeg. The job came through in September and I sat on it. I didn't want you carrying it into the match.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: Gone gone?
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Gone gone.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: Forty-one years I've known your father and he never told me.
units.name: WALT

units.text: He doesn't know either. You're the first.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: Why us? Why now?
units.name: SUNDAY

units.text: Because Teo's been lying to me about the ice for three weeks, and I figured if we're all confessing.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: It is perfectly good ice.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: It's pebbled with the wrong water, Teo. You've been using the well water since the municipal line froze. I can read it from the hack.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: It plays true.
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: It plays true. It plays true for us. It won't for them. That's why you wanted the old stones thrown first. That's why you wanted me skipping one more match.
units.name: RAINE

units.text: I wanted to win once more. Is that a crime in Manitoba?
units.name: TEODORA

units.text: Walt laughs, once, helplessly.
Priya covers her mouth.
Sunday doesn't move.
Raine rises, stiff in the knees, and walks the length of the sheet to the far house.
She sets down the broom.
Takes off a glove.
Presses her bare palm flat to the ice and holds it there while the others watch.
She stands and lifts a hand: the thumbs-up of a skip who knows the line.
